chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Leola Carter, who replaced Fats on organ at Connie's Inn
summary: Connie hired Leola Carter, a Black woman born in Bavaria, to play organ; she later became a vocal coach.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Then when he couldn't make it, then that's when there was a lady, a black woman that was born in Bavaria, Germany, and Connie got her to play the organ in Fats' place.
And her name was Leola Carter.
That's right. If you know, she used to be a vocal coach for a while. She had a studio in the Columbia -- I mean in the CBS building there on the corner of
53rd and Broadway. She used to have a studio in that building.
And she was a vocal coach --
She was educated in Germany, huh?
Uh-huh, yeah. She lived in the Alvin Hotel there when I lived there.
